before: Unreadable numeric/symbolic options were asserted false without proof.
Second-derivative classification omitted the degenerate minimum at0 of x^4-(2/3)x^6 while certifying maxima-only.
SymPy cancellation erased the exclusion x=0 in x^3/x and falsely created an initial value/extremum or full-domain simplification.
Both exact parsers imposed the convention0^0=1 without contextual authority.

after: Any unreadable option prevents this numeric/symbolic truth-vector proof.
Any zero or undecidable critical-point curvature makes this limited second-derivative family abstain.
The scientific expression/option/extrema consumers check divisors and powers before simplification, refuse unproved domains/regularity, and check the new denominator of a shift quotient.
Any candidate root whose reality is undecidable now makes the extrema family abstain.

scientific_argument: For f=x^4-(2/3)x^6, f'=4x^3(1-x^2): the sign changes from negative to positive at0, so0 is a minimum despite f''(0)=0; at±1 the second derivative is-8. The original expression x^3/x has no value at0 even though its algebraic cancellation is x^2 elsewhere. Unknown option meaning is not falsehood.
proof_limits: No domain is inferred from natural-language restrictions; supported functions are deliberately conservative.
The general algebra reader without require_total remains a syntax/expression reader, not a proof of domain identity.
This does not establish completeness of every solver family, every option grammar, or full scientific/pedagogical QCM review.
No historical/current aggregate is regenerated, no question is removed, and no human approval is written.
